name: Phu Phrabat, a testimony to the Sīma stone tradition of the Dvaravati period
description: In Ban Phue District, Udon Thani Province, in northeastern Thailand, Phu Phrabat is a hilltop park of strange, weathered rock formations. Over a thousand years ago, Buddhist monks marked out sacred ground here with upright carved stones called Sīma, and this is the world's largest surviving set still standing where it was placed. Paintings in 47 rock shelters show people lived here for some two thousand years.
